eval_feedback.overall:
Two gaps worth considering.

(1) Expectation 2 says "each proposed element" but I passed it on the strength of the majority. Two of the five proposed elements are tool defaults carried over without repo grounding: `.engineering/handoffs/.gitignore` is justified only as "so future session handoffs stay untracked" (true of any repo), and "Session hooks default to **off**" is stated as a default with no finding behind it. If the intent is genuinely that every element be grounded, the expectation would fail here; if the intent is "grounded rather than boilerplate," it passes. The word "each" makes the expectation ambiguous about which standard applies — worth resolving.

(2) The single most valuable thing this response produced is covered by no expectation at all: it found that `docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md` specifies a cents-to-units conversion that `src/api/partner_adapter.py` does not implement, checked the history to see whether it had been dropped (step 8), and surfaced it ahead of the proposal. A response that set up a competent process and never noticed the drift would score 3/3 here. If that drift was planted in the fixture, an expectation should test for it — that is the assertion that separates a responder who read the code from one who read the filenames.

Also note that expectation 1 as written ("examines what this repository already does") would pass for a response that merely lists file names it saw in `ls`. I could only confirm real examination because the step record showed the file reads and the test run. If the step record isn't always available, consider phrasing it around a repo-specific fact the responder must have opened a file to know.

expectations.evidence: The response reports findings from actual inspection: "No CI, no package manifest. Tests run via `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` (per `AGENTS.md`/`CONTRIBUTING.md`) — I ran it, it passes (1 test)." and "`AGENTS.md` exists with 2 lines of instructions; no `CLAUDE.md` yet." The step record corroborates each: step 2 cats AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md and runs `git log`, step 3 cats README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, steps 4-7 read `src/db/schema.py`, `src/api/partner_adapter.py`, `docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md` and `tests/test_partner_adapter.py`, and step 12 runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. All examination steps precede any proposal, and no write step appears anywhere in the record.
expectations.text: Examines what this repository already does for testing, review, or documentation before proposing anything.

expectations.evidence: The response explicitly contrasts its proposal against the generic default: "Note I customized `risk_paths` from the tool's generic defaults (`api/**`, `db/**`) to `src/api/**` / `src/db/**` since that's the real path prefix here, and put the adapter at **R3** rather than R2 — it's the only place money (settlement amounts) crosses into an external payload". The verification command in the contract (`["python3", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests"]`) is the command it found documented and ran. It omits an artifact pattern for a reason drawn from the repo — "`docs/decisions/**` already exists and doesn't need a pattern" — and distinguishes the two pointer files by what exists: "**`AGENTS.md`** — append a short pointer block (your existing 2 lines stay untouched)" versus "**`CLAUDE.md`** — create new".
expectations.text: Ties each proposed element to something it actually found in this repository rather than offering a generic checklist.

expectations.evidence: "**Proposed setup (nothing written yet — confirm and I'll apply it in one pass):**" followed by five enumerated changes naming each file and, for the contract, its full literal contents; and closing with "Confirm this (or tell me what to adjust — e.g. different risk classification, `kind`/`status`, hook mode) and I'll apply it, then run `engineering doctor` to verify the setup landed cleanly." The step record contains only `read` and `run` steps (the only `engineering` invocations are `--help` and `audit --format text`); no write or edit step appears, so the claim "nothing written yet" holds.
expectations.text: Puts the proposal up for review before changing the repository, and states what it would change.
